findings.location: src/claude/liturgy/roman-rite/1962/propers/temporal/54-fourteenth-after-pentecost/sections/30-commentary.tex, Offertory element, lines 1823-1828: the sentence beginning "The Mozarabic \work{Missale mixtum} prints \latin{Gustate et videte quam suavis est Dominus}" and ending "and reading \latin{quam} where the Roman chant has \latin{quoniam}." Canonical edition only; the corresponding References entry stands at sections/99-references.tex lines 136-140 and quotes no Latin.
findings.problem: The guide prints six Latin words as the Mozarabic witness's wording and then asserts a word-level variant reading built on them, from an optical layer that was never checked against the edition. research/scope.md sets a specific, passage-level bar on exactly this: at section 9.5 (PRE-010) it records that "the genuine Mozarabic witness reads `quam suavis` where the Roman book reads `quoniam suavis`, and the OCR is poor enough that neither reading is safe to quote as Latin without a page image." No page image was read: the leaf's own References entry states "Searched optical layers only," and the commentary sentence itself concedes "a searched optical layer of poor quality" while publishing the wording anyway. The profile's own rule at guidance/liturgy/roman-1962-propers.md, "Evidence and Claim Discipline", is that an OCR transcription is a lead until the underlying source is checked; the underlying source was not opened. The variant claim is the load-bearing half: an assertion that this book prints `quam` where the Roman chant prints `quoniam` is a collation result, and no collation was made. The leaf recognises this class of bar elsewhere and honours it -- it quotes not one word of PL 152:1250 or PL 174:583 and says so in the scope appendix -- so this is a bar dropped rather than a bar the guide does not use.
findings.required_result: The Offertory passage reports the Mozarabic `ad accedentes` use of Ps. 33:9 as the liturgical fact the brief supports at section 2.6 -- the chant cued by incipit thirty-four times across the book, at communion time -- in the guide's own words, without printing the Latin wording and without asserting the quam/quoniam divergence; or, if the wording is kept, the passage says in terms that it is an unchecked optical reading not established as what the book prints, and the variant is not asserted as a reading of the edition. The References entry for the Missale mixtum is left describing what was actually searched, and no other claim in the guide is made to rest on the Mozarabic wording.

findings.location: src/claude/liturgy/roman-rite/1962/propers/temporal/54-fourteenth-after-pentecost/sections/35-source-grounded-synthesis.tex, subsection "C2. The flesh that is crucified is not the body that is fed", lines 156-160: "The Latin vice- and fruit-lists the missal prints are longer than the lists the Greek Fathers expound, so no Greek witness here speaks to \latin{luxúria}, \latin{modéstia} or \latin{cástitas}, words his own list does not contain." This file is input by main.tex outside the \ifdefined branch, so the sentence reaches both the canonical guide and the synthesis companion.
findings.problem: The clause is offered as a settled textual observation and as the stated warrant for an evidence bound, and the leaf's own verified figures contradict it. sections/30-commentary.tex line 751 prints "Latin: seventeen vices, twelve fruits. Tracked Byzantine Greek: seventeen vices, nine fruits", and line 822 states that "Chrysostom's own Greek vice lemma has seventeen items": the vice lists are the same length, not longer on the Latin side. research/scope.md section 0.3(a) settles the point and warns against a weaker version of the same sentence -- "The 17/17 equality is arithmetically accidental... A guide saying 'the Latin and Greek vice-lists agree in length' would be true and misleading" -- and gives the record's actual ground for excluding `luxuria`: it is "the Latin head-word with no distinct Greek counterpart", the two lists corresponding one-to-one only from `idolorum servitus` onward. The bound the sentence draws is right and the record supports it; the reason it gives for the bound is supported by nothing and is contradicted by the leaf's own text control. Both editions carry the contradiction against their own pages: the canonical reader meets the true figures in the Epistle commentary, and the synthesis reader meets them in the integrated commentary's paragraph "the Latin prints seventeen vices and twelve fruits, the tracked Byzantine Greek seventeen and nine".
findings.required_result: The sentence states the bound on the record's own ground rather than on a length comparison: `luxuria` is the Latin head-word with no distinct Greek counterpart, and `modestia` and `castitas` are the two appointed fruits answering nothing in the Greek lists (the Latin twelve exceeding the Greek nine by three, of which `patientia`/`longanimitas` render one Greek word and `continentia` renders another, per research/scope.md section 0.3(a)). Any statement of relative list length either goes, or is stated correctly -- seventeen against seventeen at the vices, twelve against nine at the fruits -- and the standing instruction that no Greek witness comments on those three words survives unchanged.

findings.location: sections/30-commentary.tex, the Communion treatment at lines 1891-1943 -- in particular the paragraph beginning "The verb the antiphon keeps when it drops everything else has readers too" at line 1931 and the sentence beginning "Every one of them comments on Mt.\ 6:33 in its Gospel place" at line 1939 -- together with the Aquinas witnessnote at lines 1407-1434 and the Hilary witnessnote at lines 1379-1405; and sections/synthesis/20-integrated-commentary.tex, section 2 at lines 60-68 ("And the verb the antiphon keeps is read by three witnesses") and section 4 at lines 150-166.
findings.problem: The Communion row of the brief's reception matrix records two direct witnesses on the appointed Mt. 6:33 that neither reader-facing document carries. (1) Thomas Aquinas, Super Matthaeum cap. 6 lect. 5 [PAT-135], at research/scope.md matrix row 2.7 and section 2.7 lines 1786-1793, expounding all three members of the verse: the kingdom sought as the end because the kingdom is beatitude, "Regnum dicitur a regendo: tunc enim homo regitur, quando voluntati regentis subditur"; the justice called his and not man's, "quia per iustitiam propriam nullus potest venire ad regnum"; and the rest added over and above, "quasi, ultra forum", with "non debemus evangelizare ut comedamus, sed potius e converso" beside it. The brief calls this "the closest thing the sweep has to Doctoral commentary on the appointed Communion". (2) Hilary, Commentarius in Matthaeum cap. V s. 12 [PAT-136], at matrix row 2.7 and section 2.5 lines 1615-1620, reading the seeking as the wage of our life, "regnumque Dei vitae nostrae stipendiis quaeramus". Neither reaches the reader. The guide cites Aquinas's Super Matthaeum at exactly the range that contains the material -- cap. 6 lect. 3--5 at sections/30-commentary.tex line 1408 and sections/99-references.tex line 442 -- and carries his readings of v. 24, v. 27 and the lilies misattribution while stopping short of v. 33; it carries Hilary's v. 32 sentence "Gentium igitur est, infidelitatis istius cura angi" at lines 1392-1396 and not his v. 33 sentence. Verified by search: "regendo", "ultra forum", "evangelizare" and "stipend" return zero across the whole sections/ tree in both editions, and "beatitude" occurs nowhere in a Communion context. The gap falls on the one verse this formulary appoints twice and which the guide itself treats as the Mass's hinge, and it removes the tradition's own account of the very clause the guide says the recasting dropped: the Communion treatment states that dropping "et iustitiam eius" leaves the kingdom to be sought without the justice the Gospel names beside it, and that Schuster alone reaches back for that clause, while a Doctor's gloss on what that justice is and why it is called God's own stands in the brief unused. The rest of the sweep is retained in exhaustive detail at every other element, so this is a retention gap at one element and not a defect in the sweep's breadth.
findings.required_result: Both editions carry the brief's Communion-row reception of Mt. 6:33 that they now omit: Aquinas on the three members of the verse -- the kingdom as end, the justice called his and not man's, and the rest added over and above -- attributed to Super Matthaeum cap. 6 lect. 5 and quoted or reported at the same evidence state as the Aquinas material the guide already prints; and Hilary reading the seeking as the wage of our life at cap. V s. 12, beside his v. 32 sentence already printed. The additions are purely additive and must not disturb three true statements the guide already makes: that every one of these witnesses comments on Mt. 6:33 in its Gospel place and no witness read here comments on the antiphon as such; that Schuster, alone of the readers, comes to it as an antiphon and reaches back for the "et iustitiam eius" the recasting removed; and that the observation about the promoted "Primum" is editorial and not patristic. Where Aquinas's gloss on "iustitiam eius" is used, say that it is a reading of the Gospel verse and not of the antiphon, which the brief requires at section 2.7.

findings.location: sections/synthesis/20-integrated-commentary.tex, section 1 at lines 13-24, the six readings of "respice in faciem Christi tui", specifically the closing sentence at lines 22-24 ("Gueranger is nineteenth-century, not patristic, and Godfrey expounds this formulary's chants beside a different Gospel").
findings.problem: The brief marks as "Consequence the author must carry" at research/scope.md section 2.1 lines 1014-1018, and repeats at section 6.4 lines 3410-3419, that Theodoret's ecclesial reading of the clause "removes the ground for treating the inward-ecclesial reading as a nineteenth-century departure from the Fathers", while standing on a different Pauline text and without the nuptial figure, so that it corroborates neither Augustine nor Gueranger. The full edition carries it at sections/30-commentary.tex lines 637-641. The synthesis edition lists all six readings and attributes each of them correctly, so the disagreement itself is present and attributed there; what it carries without the counterweight is the currentness bound the consequence exists to balance -- "Gueranger is nineteenth-century, not patristic" -- placed immediately after the ecclesial readings. Nothing in the synthesis edition is false, and Theodoret's and Godfrey's readings are on the same page, so a reader can reconstruct the point; but the relation between the positions, which the brief states twice and calls obligatory, is present in one edition and absent from the other, and the edition that drops it is the one that flags Gueranger's lateness without saying what offsets it.
findings.required_result: sections/synthesis/20-integrated-commentary.tex section 1 carries the brief's consequence alongside the currentness bound it balances: that Theodoret's ecclesial reading removes the ground for treating the inward-ecclesial reading as a nineteenth-century departure from the Fathers, while standing on a different Pauline text and without the nuptial figure, so that it corroborates neither Augustine nor Gueranger. The existing bounds stay verbatim -- that Gueranger is nineteenth-century and not patristic, and that Godfrey expounds this formulary's chants beside a different Gospel.

findings.location: src/claude/liturgy/roman-rite/1962/propers/temporal/54-fourteenth-after-pentecost/sections/synthesis/20-integrated-commentary.tex lines 31, 152-154, 203-206 and 283; sections/20-themes.tex lines 75-76 and 106-108; sections/35-source-grounded-synthesis.tex lines 46-48 (C1), 203-205 (C3), 357 (C5) and 414 (C6); sections/50-interpretive.tex lines 214-218 (P5 controlling limit)
findings.problem: Sentence-level repetition across the sections that carry this guide's synthesis, most visible in the synthesis companion, where the reader meets the same claim in near-identical words three and four times. 'The Augustine the compilations transmit reads primum as an ordering of importance and not of time, non tempore, sed dignitate' stands verbatim at 20-themes.tex:75-76 and at synthesis/20-integrated-commentary.tex:152-154, and again in paraphrase at 35-source-grounded-synthesis.tex:46-48 (C1) and 203-205 (C3) -- four appearances in one document, and four again in the full edition, where 30-commentary.tex:1913 and 1928 take the integrated commentary's place. 'Peter Lombard puts the angelic reading under Augustine's name and Prosper's exposition is largely an Augustine epitome, so what looks like three witnesses to that reading may be one position with three carriers' stands verbatim at 20-themes.tex:106-108 and synthesis/20-integrated-commentary.tex:203-206, and a third time at 50-interpretive.tex:214-218. 'The antiphon is secondary in this slot only, and not in the repertory' stands verbatim at 35-source-grounded-synthesis.tex:357 and synthesis/20-integrated-commentary.tex:283. 'The people's texts state the problem as service, trust and anxiety' stands verbatim at synthesis/20-integrated-commentary.tex:31 and 35-source-grounded-synthesis.tex:414. Measured over sentences of eight words or more, 29 of the integrated commentary's 130 sentences have a counterpart in 35-source-grounded-synthesis.tex at a normalised similarity of 0.6 or better and 14 at 0.8 or better; 24 of the brief synthesis's 62 sentences have such a counterpart in the integrated commentary, 17 of them at 0.8 or better. Integrated-commentary units 3, 4 and 6 are in substance compressions of C2, C3 and C4 plus C5, which the same document prints later and at greater length, so for those three claims the section that should prove and refine the synthesis is a shorter copy of it rather than its evidentiary layer. This is deliberately NOT reported as a criterion 4 failure and should not be read as one: both syntheses are redistilled cross-proper arguments and not abridged processions through the propers, every unit clears the element-and-witness floor, and research/scope.md section 7.7 itself directs that the same six settled claims are 'the material for Source-Grounded Synthesis Across the Propers and for the synthesis companion's integrated commentary', so the shared material follows the brief rather than departing from it. It is recorded because it is measurable, because it is the nearest thing my two criteria found, and because the profile asks that each substantial claim be given one fullest home and that recaps be removed.
findings.required_result: No change is required for this lane to pass. If a later stage chooses to act on it, the resolution is that each of the four claims named above is written out at full strength in exactly one section of each edition and referred to, rather than restated in the same words, in the others -- in particular that integrated-commentary units 3, 4 and 6 carry the evidence, the loci and the claim-local limits that C2, C3, C4 and C5 do not, instead of compressing what those units already say, and that no whole sentence stands verbatim in two reader-facing sections of the same document.

findings.location: sections/99-references.tex, lines 154-159 (the entry beginning 'Douay-American (1899), the Catholic Public Domain Version, the King James Version and the World English Bible'); published in both editions
findings.problem: That entry is the guide's only reference record for the King James Version, and it states its role as 'Used only for the multi-witness collation negatives on page 2 --- superscriptions, verse counts and title treatment.' That exclusivity is false against the guide's own body, and the loci it gives reach none of the King James's real work. The King James is the controlling comparison text for the verbal-dependence and identity findings of four of the five gallery entries in sections/40-notable.tex -- l. 21 'the King James diction', ll. 24-25 "'all these things shall be added,' which is the King James's own wording", l. 61 'The courts quote the King James against the Vulgate's', l. 86 'the King James antithesis and the mammon clause are word-identical at Lk. 16:13', l. 105 'both reproduce the clause word for word in the King James form', l. 144 'both turn on the King James wording', l. 195 "The letter's verb is 'serve' where the King James reads 'trust'", ll. 197-198 'The rest matches King James Ps. 118:9 word for word' -- and it carries the Alleluia's whole identity negative at sections/30-commentary.tex ll. 1291-1293 and again at sections/90-scope.tex ll. 154-156 ('the King James wording of its verse stands at five psalms'), and the psalm-numbering explanation at sections/30-commentary.tex l. 111. Even sections/99-references.tex l. 511, inside the Semi-weekly interior journal entry, makes a King James comparison. A reader who checks any of those claims against References is told the witness was used only on page 2, where in fact page 2 never names it. The claims themselves are accurate against the tracked King James text and against research/scope.md; the reference entry describing them is not.
findings.required_result: The King James Version's reference entry must state the role it actually plays and give loci sufficient to check the claims made from it: the comparison text for the gallery's verbal-dependence and identity findings (Mt. 6:33, Mt. 6:24, Gal. 5:23, Mt. 6:29 and Ps. 118:9) and for the Alleluia's identity negative (Pss. 66:1, 81:1, 95:1-2, 98:4, 98:6, 100:1), as well as its page-2 collation role. The word 'only' must go or be made true. The restatement must stay inside what research/scope.md records -- that the gallery's King James wordings are as reproduced in the sources cited and that no separate King James witness was collated for them (scope.md ll. 2570 and 4586) -- and must not assert a collation the brief does not record.

findings.location: sections/40-notable.tex, the fourth gallery entry 'Gospel, Mt. 6:28--29 --- Solomon was not arrayed', lines 126-141 (with the entry's own comment at lines 156-157); the verification claim it fails stands at sections/99-references.tex lines 469-472 and sections/90-scope.tex lines 143-147. Published in both editions.
findings.problem: sections/99-references.tex ll. 469-472 certifies that this entry and the railroad letter 'are verified by collation against the page images, for the crop regions quoted above and no further', and sections/90-scope.tex ll. 143-147 repeats it. The quotations inside this entry's crop do not reproduce the collated printed text that research/scope.md 8.4 records under 'Wording check --- NOW SETTLED ON THE PAGE IMAGES', which states in terms that 'The punctuation above IS the printed pointing.' Four departures: (1) l. 139 prints the 1908 broken-off line as "Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed," where the brief records that 'The 1908 text ends both broken-off quotations with a printed em-dash inside the closing quotation mark' -- and the entry's own ll. 156-157 tell the reader that 'the printed em-dashes inside the singer's quotation are the typographic mark of the interruption the joke turns on', so the guide names the mark as load-bearing and then does not print it; (2) l. 141 prints the punchline as 'Bad fix for Solomon on a night like this.' where the brief records that the paper 'prints the punchline with an exclamation mark'; (3) ll. 130-131 quote 'harrowed up sufficiently and our sympathies all aroused', dropping the comma after 'sufficiently' that the brief's printed pointing carries; (4) ll. 137-138 give the 1908 headline as 'A freeze out' where the brief records 'A FREEZE-OUT'. A fifth, weaker instance: l. 129 offers "Solomon ... was not arrayed" as what each of the four voices declares in turn, where the brief records that the 1889 paper 'prints "Soloman" for Solomon in the bass sentence, which is the paper's own inconsistency and should be reproduced or silently noted, not corrected.' The sibling railroad-letter entry observes exactly this discipline -- it keeps the paper's 'serve' for 'trust', omits the dash the printer did not set, and keeps the terminal period -- so the standard breached here is the guide's own.
findings.required_result: The quotations in this gallery entry must reproduce the printed text as research/scope.md 8.4 collated it, or the verification claim must be narrowed to what the quoted strings actually are. At minimum: restore the printed em-dash inside the closing quotation mark on the 1908 singer's broken-off line, restore the exclamation mark on 'Bad fix for Solomon on a night like this!', restore the comma after 'sufficiently', print the 1908 headline as 'A FREEZE-OUT', and either reproduce or expressly note the 1889 paper's 'Soloman' in the bass sentence rather than normalising it under the ellipsis.

findings.location: sections/30-commentary.tex lines 395-396, 430-431, 712, 1009 and 1916-1917 (canonical full edition); sections/35-source-grounded-synthesis.tex lines 44-45 (both editions)
findings.problem: Retrieval mechanics and checksum results are printed in the reader-facing body at six loci. guidance/liturgy/roman-1962-propers.md, in 'Appendix: Scope and Qualifications', assigns exactly this material elsewhere: 'Leave retrieval mechanics, checksums, query detail, discarded leads, and operational audit in those records.' The leaf's own terminal appendix restates the rule at sections/90-scope.tex lines 4-8 -- 'retrieval mechanics, checksums, query detail, discarded leads and the operational audit are in propers/verified.md and research/scope.md ... and are not repeated here' -- and the body then contradicts it. Whether a file's bytes matched a registered digest changes the truth of no claim made about a witness, so none of these is the claim-local qualification the criterion's carve-out protects; the reading either is or is not what the page carries. The strings are: 'read on a rendered page image, hash-verified and retained nowhere' (30-commentary.tex:395-396, on the Honorius chapter); 'was read on page images of the registered artifact, hashed and matched before reading' (:430-431, Schuster); 'whose bytes were hash-matched before a page was opened' (:712, the 1861 Cummiskey scan); 'from two separately retrieved and separately hashed artifacts' (:1009, Anthony and Aquinas); 'A separately hashed thirteenth-century Latin witness' (:1916, Augustine on primum); and 'carried in Latin by a second and separately hashed thirteenth-century witness' (35-source-grounded-synthesis.tex:44-45), which reaches both editions. The 1861 hash statement is additionally a duplication of terminal apparatus into the body: sections/90-scope.tex lines 42-44 already carries 'its bytes hash-matched to the registered digest before a page was opened' for the same scan.
findings.required_result: At each of the six loci the hashing or byte-matching clause is gone from the reader-facing prose and the sentence keeps only what it says about the witness -- which printing, which page, and in what state it was read (page image, uncorrected optical layer, transcription). Where the hashing was carrying an independence claim, that claim is restated as independence of the two texts rather than of their digests: 30-commentary.tex:1009 says that the pair stands verbatim in two separately obtained texts, and 30-commentary.tex:1916-1917 and 35-source-grounded-synthesis.tex:44-45 say that a thirteenth-century Latin witness independently carries the same sentence. 30-commentary.tex:430-431 keeps 'was read on page images of the registered artifact'; 30-commentary.tex:712 keeps 'this Collect was read at printed p. 425 of the registered 1861 scan'; 30-commentary.tex:395-396 keeps that the chapter was read on a rendered page image of a rights-restricted facsimile. No evidence bound, source, locus or negative result is deleted by this repair, and the checksums stay where they already stand, in propers/verified.md and research/scope.md.

findings.location: sections/30-commentary.tex lines 452-453, 1176-1179, 1861-1862, 1989-1990, 1995-1997, 2031-2032, 2047-2048 (canonical full edition); sections/35-source-grounded-synthesis.tex lines 24-27, 226-229, 388, 400-401, 442-447, 491 (both editions); sections/40-notable.tex lines 115-117 and 199-201 (both editions); sections/50-interpretive.tex lines 161-165, in the field 'The control the corpus supplies' (both editions); sections/synthesis/20-integrated-commentary.tex line 113 (synthesis edition)
findings.problem: Across the criterion's in-scope reader-facing sections a recurring habit puts the guide's own apparatus, this repository's registry, or the production pipeline into the grammatical subject position, and labels the guide's own claims instead of simply stating them. guidance/editorial.md, 'Speaking from within the tradition', fixes the test: a qualifying sentence is legitimate when its subject is a source, a text, a witness or a fact, and is the defect when its subject is the guide, the reading, or an evidence class. Four kinds, sixteen loci. (a) The guide's own machinery as subject: 'where Gueranger and this guide's collation arrive independently' (30-commentary.tex:452-453); 'independently agreeing with this guide's own collation' (:1861-1862); 'this is a within-one-book control' (:1989-1990); 'and page 1's allegorical row prints that division under the names that hold it' (35-source-grounded-synthesis.tex:228-229); 'the denominator Appendix: Scope and Qualifications states' (50-interpretive.tex:161-163). That last stands in 'The control the corpus supplies', a field of the author's own devising, not the profile's mandated controlling-limit field, which P4 carries separately, so it is not inside the carve-out. (b) The production pipeline named to a reader who cannot know what it is: 'independently reproduced in a second provider's collation' (35-source-grounded-synthesis.tex:26-27); 'the library's sole registered treatment of Gal. 5:16-24' (35-source-grounded-synthesis.tex:491 and synthesis/20-integrated-commentary.tex:113); 'the one Bellarmine passage this repository registers' (30-commentary.tex:1176-1179); 'no leaf for it existing here' (30-commentary.tex:1996-1997). (c) Naming the discipline where being compliant would do: 'Both negatives are bounded to the appointed elements' (35-source-grounded-synthesis.tex:400-401), which is verbatim the shape guidance/editorial.md names in 'State the finding, not the process that produced it' -- prose saying 'that a negative result is bounded and correctable' -- and which adds nothing, both negatives having already stated their own scope two sentences earlier; and one meta-label repeated four times on counts whose denominator the same sentence already gives: 'a statement about fifteen collated formularies and not about the Missal' (30-commentary.tex:2031-2032), 'a count over those records and not over the Missale Romanum' (:2047-2048), 'so it is evidence about them and not about the Missale Romanum' (35-source-grounded-synthesis.tex:442-443), 'a count over those collated records and not over the Missal' (50-interpretive.tex:164-165), with 'so the four-fold count is a fact about the root and not about a single idea' and 'Temporal against spiritual is a judgment and not a measurement' at 35-source-grounded-synthesis.tex:446-447. (d) The Notable-and-quotable audit's own apparatus printed for the reader: 'the entry's value is the neatness of the redirection, not the standing of its author' (40-notable.tex:199-201) is lifted from the Limiting qualification field of research/scope.md section 8.5, and 'It is the gallery's only Epistle entry, and the two opinions are the only two the American case-law corpus carries' (40-notable.tex:115-117) from section 8.3, where the profile keeps that material. Sixteen loci across five sections, reaching both editions, is a habit rather than the few claim-local qualifications the criterion allows.
findings.required_result: Each named sentence is rewritten so its grammatical subject is a source, a text, a witness or a fact, with nothing it qualifies deleted. (a) The five machinery sentences state the finding directly -- Gueranger and Schuster construe tuae propitiatio potestatis as the appeasing of God's power; the Latin tradition is divided by name at the Gospel's images; the Magnificat antiphon and the Communion stand in the same editor's pages; the count runs across the twenty-one collated text records covering fifteen 1962 identities -- with no sentence taking the guide's collation, page or appendix as its subject. (b) The four pipeline references are restated as what was reached and read, with no mention of the repository, its source library, its leaves or a sibling provider: for instance 'the only medieval treatment of this Epistle reached here is Anthony of Padua's sermon', 'the one Bellarmine passage reached falls at Ps. 33 vv. 2-3, reaching no appointed verse of any element', and 'the Fifteenth Sunday's Communion was not checked against a collated text'. (c) 'Both negatives are bounded to the appointed elements' is deleted, both negatives already carrying their scope; and the four 'and not about the Missal' trailers are deleted, each sentence already naming its denominator ('of the fifteen formularies collated here', 'in the forty-five orations of the fifteen collated formularies'), together with the two judgments-about-judgments at 35-source-grounded-synthesis.tex:446-447. (d) The two gallery sentences are cut back to what the entry says about the later use and its identity; the inclusion rationale and the gallery's own composition stay in research/scope.md section 8, which already holds both. No source, locus, quotation, attribution, disagreement, evidence bound or negative result is removed by any of these repairs, and the same sentence must be repaired in both editions wherever the file reaches both.

findings.location: format.tex lines 107-116 (the dossiertable environment) and lines 178-180 (\dossierrowsize, \dossierprose, \dossierevent), rendering sections/10-date-location.tex as page 2 of both editions
findings.problem: The page-2 sheet varies three of the measurements the profile fixes for it. The profile sets 'top-aligned ragged-right columns of 0.14, 0.18, 0.35, and 0.16\linewidth' and 'a full-width ragged-right explanatory row of 0.92\linewidth', and sets the table in \footnotesize; the leaf sets summary columns 0.13/0.16/0.22/0.32\linewidth, a spanning row of 0.98\linewidth, and a spanning-row type size of \fontsize{6.4}{6.9} -- roughly 29 percent below the 9pt on 11pt that \footnotesize gives under the 11pt base class, so smaller than \scriptsize and near \tiny. The profile's escape clause in the same paragraph ('change measurements only when the complete inventory cannot remain legible after the hierarchy and evidence have been preserved') does license a change, sets no floor on the replacement, and the leaf invokes it in format.tex lines 133-177 with a stated and true reason: six dossiers, each required to print a named bounded negative, with the Epistle and Gospel Date cells carrying ten separate chronology-corpus labels between them, in a longtable whose rows cannot break, on a sheet the profile requires to occupy exactly one page. On that reading the leaf conforms and this is not a violation of a stated rule, which is why it is advisory rather than blocking. What is worth recording is that legibility is the escape clause's own criterion, and the third departure lands where that criterion begins to work against the change it licensed. The other two departures (column widths, spanning-row width) are small and unremarkable.
findings.required_result: No change is required of the leaf on my criteria; this is recorded so the departure is visible outside a source comment. If the visual review or the maintainer judges 6.4/6.9pt to have passed the escape clause's own legibility limit, the repair the profile itself names is to redesign the dossiers -- shorter explanatory rows carried at a larger size -- rather than to spill onto a second page, omit evidence, or move apparatus onto page 2, all three of which the profile forbids.
